S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal event causing injury, evacuation, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete report within 10 business days. Less severe thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator in a quarterly aggregate, with model and incident details. Customers whose unit was involved must be notified within 24 hours; customers in an affected installation or batch must receive a safety notice within 5 business days when a credible safety risk is identified.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires prompt submission of a corrective-action plan and retesting; it does not by itself require an immediate sales ban. Before purchase, customers must receive the model's test protocol, sample size, failure count, failure rate, and a plain-language explanation of results and precautions. These results must not be publicly disclosed by the standard.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: For already-installed units, manufacturers must offer a retrofit or equivalent mitigation plan within 6 years of this standard taking effect; units that cannot be safely retrofitted must receive an appropriate alternative safety measure and customer notice.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery systems placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard is adopted.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide incident data, an investigation, and a proposed corrective-action plan. The threshold triggers prompt regulator review and a documented decision on corrective action; it does not by itself require automatic recall.

document.section_notes: The final text drops automatic sales bans for models above 5% (S2) and automatic recall at 8 per 100k (S5), each of which protects one company's flagship (Hearth 10 and Ember 8, respectively). Reporting of less severe thermal incidents moves to a quarterly aggregate, which is weaker than the 30-day benchmark. Remote shut-off retrofit (6 years) and built-in suppression (36 months) both fall in the acceptable band.
